documents.content:
Sorting

AC Grid provides powerful sorting capabilities that allow users to organize data by clicking column headers.

 Quick Start

Sorting is enabled by default in AC Grid. Users can simply click column headers to sort data.



 Basic Usage

 Enabling Sorting

Sorting is enabled by default. To disable sorting on specific columns, set enableSorting: false.



 Single Column Sorting

 User Interaction

When users click a column header, the sort state cycles through:

1. Unsorted → Click → Ascend

documents.title: grid-state
documents.content:
Grid state

Grid exposes getState, setState, and resetState on the element returned by createGrid. The versioned state includes column widths and order, sorting, filters, pagination, and vertical scroll position.



Pass partial state to setState; omitted fields keep their current values. getState returns a snapshot with stateVersion: 1 suitable for JSON serialization.

documents.title: Accessibility
documents.content:
Accessibility

AC Grid exposes its table as an ARIA grid with row, column-header, and cell semantics. Give each grid a useful name so screen-reader users can identify it.



ariaLabel and ariaDescription can also be assigned as properties on <wsx-ac-grid>. Column accessible names default to the text header or the column ID when the header is not plain text; ariaLabel and ariaDescription on a column override that fallback. Getting Started with AC Grid

AC Grid is a fully open source data grid to replace AG Grid. It's framework-agnostic, built with Web Components and @tanstack/table-corehttps://tanstack.com/table/latest.

 Installation



 Quick Start

 With a bundler Vite, Webpack, etc.
